divergence_scope.divergence_denominator: distinct QUESTION KINDS, not distinct prompts and not total asks
divergence_scope.why: a deterministic body re-asked a byte-identical question answers it identically by construction, so total asks is the wrong denominator. So is distinct PROMPTS: a frontier that refills itself with indexed probes produces fifty distinct prompts and seven distinct questions. The scope of any divergence claim is the question-kind count

materially_participated.publishable_finding: model choices never diverged from the fixed policy across 13 DISTINCT QUESTION KINDS (13 distinct prompts, 13 asks, 0 byte-identical repeats). That is a finding about this resident on this frontier, not a decorated timeline - and the scope is the KIND count, because a deterministic body cannot disagree with itself on the same question and an indexed probe series is one question asked many times
materially_participated.why: no choose() diverged from the fixed policy; no model decision changed what ran next

participation.token_count_authority: native-resident protocol fields; not a throughput claim
participation.why_two_fractions: divergence is UNDEFINED on a menu of one. The clock outran the real catalog, so most cycles offered a single auto-generated probe and counting them as agreement scores a choice nobody was given. The second fraction is over cycles where two or more options existed; null means there were none, which is a statement about the FRONTIER, not about the resident.
